classification.difficultyReason: Apply the sine rule and explain why a calculated sine value rules out a triangle.

content.prompt: Try to find the angle $\theta$ in this triangle; explain why it is impossible.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7, triangle below the instruction on the left
spec.description: Horizontal base, upper vertex toward the left, side labels 10 and 25, and marked base angles θ and 30°. No fill.
spec.mathematics: The side opposite θ is 25 and the side opposite 30° is 10. These numerical givens are inconsistent with a triangle; the illustration preserves the source's schematic arrangement without claiming metric accuracy.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\theta}{25}&=\frac{\sin30^{\circ}}{10}\\\sin\theta&=\frac{25\sin30^{\circ}}{10}\\\sin\theta&=1.25\end{align*}$$
This is impossible because a sine value cannot exceed $1$. Therefore, there is no possible angle $\theta$, and such a triangle cannot be constructed.
